pages.text: Evening. The room smells of tea. Minena has brought a cup and spilled half of it. The others sit on the floor, on the bed, on your feet.
“Tell us about the farm that burned down!” “Again?” you say. “Yes!” “And don't forget the bells,” whispers someone very small. “Shh! That comes later!”
You close your eyes. You are not sure you remember it right. But it always begins the same way: with ash.
Everything is grey. Ash, mud, black posts where a house once stood. The farm of your family is gone.
But look. One green patch in the ash. On it stands one ripe wheat stalk. Every grain has been nibbled off. All but one.
You pick up the last grain. Somebody was here. And somebody left it for you.
The book in the box is old. On the first page, in thin brown ink: “Start small. Small is plenty.”
You read it twice. Then, from nowhere, an old tune comes back, and a line of words: “Long ears sow the clover green.”
The first night. The sky is huge. At the edge of the dark forest, white stones glow, very faintly.
Somewhere, a tune. You do not know it. You find you are humming it anyway.

c1_bells.title: A little bell
c1_bells.text: When the last thistle is out, you hear it: a tiny bell, high in the air. Then nothing. Behind you, three sticks lie in a very silly pile. Nothing is missing.

c1_ledger.title: A burnt page
c1_ledger.text: Under the black boards you find a page, burnt at the edges. A list of numbers. At the bottom, in red: “The Lord's share.” Every year the red number is bigger. You fold the page small and keep it.

pages.text: A cart creaks along the old track and stops by your land. The seller sniffs. “Is that porridge?” You hand her a bowl. She eats it standing up, very fast.
“You're from Moonedge, aren't you?” she says. “Good porridge, {player}. I'll tell them in the village that somebody is cooking up here again.”

c1_board.title: The notice board
c1_board.text: A notice board, full of little papers. Somebody needs a basket. Somebody has lost a goat. You read every one twice, and keep your hat low.

pages.text: A bunny sits on the one green patch. She sits like someone who has always sat there.
Now you understand. The patch stayed green because somebody looked after it. The stalk was nibbled because somebody was hungry. And one grain was left for you.
Now the first line of the old rhyme makes sense: “Long ears sow the clover green.” You say it out loud. The bunny's ear twitches.

c1_bell_out.title: Two soft rings
c1_bell_out.text: That night, from far away: two soft rings of a very small bell. You sit up in the dark. The bunny is asleep in the clover. So who else is still here?

pages.text: Back in the room, the tea has gone cold. “Was there really a bunny?” asks Minena. “There was,” you say. “She was very rude about carrots.”
“And the bell? Who rang the bell?” “Shh!” says everybody at once. “That's next time!” You smile. They know this story almost as well as you do. Almost.

c1_k_seller.text: “Do you ever stop?” calls the seller from the track. You wave. You do not stop.

c1_k_hens.text: The hens argue about who laid which egg. Nobody wins.

c1_k_bucket.text: The old bucket clanks against the well stones. It sounds almost proud.

c1_k_grass.text: Something rustles in the long grass. It stops when you look.

c1_k_smoke.text: The wind still smells a little of old smoke.

c1_k_winter.text: The tent flaps in the wind. You pull the blanket up to your nose.
